theorems.name: Topology Axioms
theorems.statement: A topology \tau on X contains \emptyset,X, is closed under arbitrary unions, and closed under FINITE intersections.
theorems.conditions: The finite qualifier on intersections is essential.
theorems.intuition: Infinite intersections of open sets can collapse to non-open sets (e.g. single points), so only finite intersection-closure is required.
theorems.proofSketch: N/A — this is the definition itself.
theorems.example: \cap_{n=1}^\infty (-1/n,1/n) = {0}, not open in R, showing why infinite intersection-closure isn't required.
theorems.examReady: State all three axioms; emphasize 'finite' for intersections.

theorems.name: Closed Set Properties
theorems.statement: \emptyset, X are closed; arbitrary intersections of closed sets are closed; FINITE unions of closed sets are closed.
theorems.conditions: Dual to the open-set axioms via De Morgan's laws.
theorems.intuition: Complementing an open-set statement flips unions and intersections.
theorems.proofSketch: Apply De Morgan's laws to the topology axioms.
theorems.example: [1/n,1] union over all n gives (0,1], not closed — showing infinite unions of closed sets can fail.
theorems.examReady: Derive directly from the open-set axioms via complementation.
